proposal.hypothesis: Four warps per block cover one 32×32 input tile as 8×32 strips. Each lane first owns eight row values for its input column; four 8-lane groups then transpose their 8×8 subtiles by swapping lane/register bits with warp-local XOR shuffles. This should produce coalesced input loads and contiguous 8-float store segments without shared memory or a block barrier. The extra shuffle instructions and segmented stores may offset that benefit, so candidate timing is needed.

retained: Replace the active naive kernel launch with a 32×4-thread block; each warp loads an 8×32 strip, with all lanes loading eight rows at adjacent columns.

Transpose each 8×8 lane/register subgroup through three lane-bit/register-bit exchange stages. Each pair uses a same-warp XOR shuffle with width 8; no cross-warp exchange, shared memory, or CTA barrier is used.
Store the transposed values as eight contiguous floats per subgroup, using unsigned bit-preserving shuffles and float bitcasts for exact copies; use size_t offsets for matrix indexing.
